title: Singapore's Assessment of 20-Point Peace Plan for Gaza
what_it_is: Singapore's Assessment of 20-Point Peace Plan for Gaza

sections.label: Singapore welcomes Israel-Hamas agreement
sections.summary: Singapore welcomed the 9 October 2025 agreement by Israel and Hamas on the first phase of the Trump peace plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore welcomed the agreement that was reached on 9 October 2025 by Israel and Hamas on the first phase of the Trump peace plan.

sections.label: First phase implementation and next steps
sections.summary: America's leverage brought the first phase, now being implemented with a ceasefire and hostage release, followed by humanitarian aid, a Transitional Authority and Palestinian Authority reform toward a two-state solution Singapore supports.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But the fact is that America remains the indispensable superpower with real leverage and is willing to apply that leverage on the warring parties to arrive at where we are today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, the first phase is now being implemented and in particular, that means a ceasefire and the release of the hostages, at least, those who are alive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The next few essential steps are a surge in humanitarian assistance – and I will explain later what Singapore will do on that front – and then, the establishment of some kind of Transitional Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And then, the Palestinian Authority, which as part of that plan, has committed to reform.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And I will also explain what we will do to assist the Palestinian Authority on its journey and, on its journey, which I would like to add, ultimately, to a two-state solution, which Singapore supports.

sections.label: Transitional Authority and Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: It is premature to discuss the Transitional Authority, which is still inchoate, but in the immediate term Singapore wants to do more with the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is premature to discuss what we will do with the Transitional Authority, because that is still inchoate at this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But what I would say, is that, in the short term, in the immediate term, we certainly want to do more with the Palestinian Authority.

sections.label: Peacekeeping troops premature, awaiting UN resolution
sections.summary: It is premature to talk about peacekeeping troops, and Singapore would wait first for a UN Security Council resolution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, these are things again and I see where the Member is coming from, but let us be realistic and approach this in a step wise fashion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is premature to talk about peacekeeping troops.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As I said, I would wait first for a UN Security Council resolution.

sections.label: Twenty-point plan and two-state solution
sections.summary: The 20-point plan is a great achievement, and Singapore believes Palestinians have a right to self determination and there should be a negotiated two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The 20-point plan, as the Member has said, is a great achievement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore believes the Palestinians have a right to self determination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore believes there should be a negotiated two-state solution.

sections.label: Quietly helpful, cooperating with Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: Singapore's approach is to do more, say less and be quietly helpful, so it is not asking to sit on any boards but will step up cooperation with the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Our approach is always to do more, say less, be quietly helpful and constructive work from the ground up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, that is why we are not asking to sit on any boards, but we will step up our long-standing cooperation with the Palestinian Authority.

sections.label: Transitional Authority coordination reference
sections.summary: The speaker says he would take reference from the soon-to-be established Transitional Authority, with people on the ground deciding needs and coordinating.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I would also take reference from the hopefully soon-to-be established Transitional Authority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is for people on the ground to decide what is needed and to coordinate, and then we fit in.

sections.label: Singapore contributions to Palestinian Authority
sections.summary: Asked whether Singapore will join 12 nations contributing financially to the Palestinian Authority, the Minister says it is premature but he would share a specific programme if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister, 12 nations, including France and Japan, have set up an emergency coalition for the financial sustainability of the Palestinian Authority to support the effort to stabilise the Palestinian Authority's finances and ensure the continued viability of the two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In light of the Gaza Peace Plan, will Singapore now consider joining them in making financial contributions to the Palestinian Authority, and if not, why not?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think it is premature, but if the need arises and if there is a specific programme, I will certainly be happy to share it with the House.
